items.title: Section: The Abode With Applied Effort, Having No Further Mark, Opens — Ten Skilful Wisdoms, the First Five

items.zh: 云何菩薩有加行有功用無相住？謂諸菩薩於前第六緣起相應增上慧住，已得十種妙方便慧所引世間不共一切有情，而共一切世間進道勝行。
items.en:
Eighth abode, with applied effort, having no further mark; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode with applied effort, having no further mark?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, entry brought to fulfilment through uncommon, excellent conduct; first, clarifying entry. Namely, bodhisattvas, previously at the sixth abode joined with dependent origination, have already attained ten kinds of wondrous, skilful wisdom.
Commentary: Regarding "ten kinds of wondrous, skilful wisdom" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if a bodhisattva, having well accomplished the conduct of the sixth ground, wishes to enter the seventh bodhisattva ground, should arouse excellent conduct through ten skilful means. What are the ten? Namely: well cultivating emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, while gathering great, supportive merit for the path. Entering the selflessness of persons, absence of a life-force, absence of sentient beings, while never abandoning the arousal of the four immeasurables. Arousing meritorious dharmas, undertaking heightened perfection-conduct, while grasping at no dharma whatsoever. Attaining departure from the three realms, while still able to manifest conduct adorning the three realms. Utterly, quiescently extinguishing every blaze of affliction, while still able to arouse, for every sentient being's sake, conduct extinguishing the blaze of craving, hatred, and delusion.

items.title: Section: Four Underlying Excellences Gathering All Ten Wisdoms — Wealth, Guarding Against Evil, Guarding Wholesome Roots, and Gathering Beings

items.zh: 即由如是妙方便慧所引不共進道勝行成上品故，極圓滿故，超過第六住，得入第七住。
items.en:
Commentary: Regarding "arousing world-flourishing" and the like — the Commentary on the Ten Grounds Sutra says: this excellent conduct has four kinds of merit. First, excellence in wealth and body — freely able to obtain whatever is needed. Second, excellence in guarding against evil — never abandoning sentient beings, arousing the four immeasurables. Third, excellence in guarding wholesome roots — diligently cultivating correct conduct, grasping at not even the slightest dharma. Fourth, excellence in gathering sentient beings, itself further divided: taking rebirth according to vow, in order not to abandon sentient beings; furthermore, skilfully teaching the true dharma, so that all sentient beings might permanently extinguish afflictive conduct; furthermore, extinguishing only defilement, never extinguishing conditioned activity, undertaking immeasurable deeds; furthermore, adorning every buddha-land, for the sake of gathering together the great assembly of the true dharma; furthermore, knowing the Tathāgata to be without mark, without sound, without any conceptual discrimination, yet possessing every kind of resembling manifestation, so that sentient beings may see, approach, make offerings, and cultivate merit, and for the sake of turning the dharma-wheel, skilfully answering whatever is asked.
By this same wondrous, skilful wisdom's uncommon, excellent conduct becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, one passes beyond the sixth abode and enters the seventh.

items.title: Section: The Tenfold Restatement — Relying on World-Flourishing, Benefiting Beings, and the Tathāgata's Own Body, Voice, and Mind

items.zh: 如是文詞，如經廣說，應知其相。謂依能起世間興盛攝受福德；依於有情利益安樂增上意樂；依為菩提，福德資糧、菩提分法後後勝進；依不共聲聞；依不共獨覺；依有情界；依諸法界；依諸世界；依諸如來身語心智。當知是名妙方便慧所引不共進道勝行處所略義。
items.en: Second, pointing to the brief meaning. This wording, exactly as the sutra explains at length; one should understand its mark accordingly. Namely, relying on what is able to give rise to world-flourishing and gather merit; relying on heightened aspiration for the benefit and ease of sentient beings; relying on provisions of merit for the sake of awakening, and ever-further advancement in the factors of awakening; relying on what is uncommon to hearers; relying on what is uncommon to solitary-realisers; relying on the realm of sentient beings; relying on the realm of dharmas; relying on the realm of worlds; relying on the Tathāgatas' own body, voice, mind, and wisdom. One should understand this as the brief meaning of the ground on which wondrous, skilful wisdom's uncommon, excellent conduct rests.

items.title: Section: Penetrating the Buddhas' Own State, Arousing Diligent Applied Effort Towards the Eighth Ground

items.zh: 菩薩與彼共相應故，便能通達無量無數如來境界，及為彼起無功用、無相、無分別、無異分別觀無量佛境界，起無間無缺精勤修學一切威儀行住作意，一切分位不遠離道。
items.en: Second aspect: penetrating the buddhas' own state, arousing diligent applied effort. Such a bodhisattva, corresponding fully to this excellent conduct, is thereby able to penetrate the immeasurable, countless state of the tathāgatas, and, in order to observe that state, gives rise to conduct without effortful application, without mark, without discrimination, without variant discrimination, observing the buddhas' own immeasurable state — arousing, without interruption or deficiency, diligent cultivation of every bodily deportment, whether walking or standing, constantly bringing attention to bear, never departing, in any circumstance whatsoever, from the path.

items.title: Section: Every Single Instant Fully Realises the Factors of Awakening — Each Ground's Own Distinguishing Excellence Reviewed

items.zh: 彼於一一心剎那中，十波羅蜜多而為上首，一切菩提分法圓滿殊勝。諸餘下住則不如是。謂於第一極歡喜住，正以大願為勝所緣；於第二住，正能除遣毀犯戒垢；於第三住，正願增長，得法光明；於第四住，正趣入道；於第五住，正入一切世間事業；於第六住，正入甚深緣起道理；今即於此第七住中，具足發起一切佛法覺支圓滿。
items.en:
Third aspect: every single instant fully realises the factors of awakening; first, distinguishing this ground. In every single instant of mind, the ten perfections taken as foremost, every factor belonging to awakening is completely, excellently fulfilled. Every ground below this one is not yet so.
Second, an explanatory review. At the first, utmost joy, the great vow is the most excellent object. At the second, correctly removing every stain of precept violation. At the third, correct vows increasing, attaining the light of dharma. At the fourth, correctly entering the path. At the fifth, correctly entering every kind of worldly undertaking. At the sixth, correctly entering the profound principle of dependent origination. Now, at this seventh ground, every buddha-dharma's own factor of awakening is fully, completely aroused.

items.title: Section: Applied-Effort Conduct Now Complete — the Direct Threshold Into the Eighth Ground's Utmost Purity

items.zh: 此住菩薩加行行圓滿所攝故；妙智神通行清淨，能入第八住故。由是菩薩此住無間，能入第八極清淨住。
items.en: Fourth aspect: subsumed within the complete fulfilment of applied-effort conduct. A bodhisattva at this abode is subsumed within the complete fulfilment of applied-effort conduct. The conduct of wondrous wisdom and spiritual power is genuinely pure, able to enter the eighth abode. By this, such a bodhisattva, without any further interval, is able to enter the eighth abode of utmost purity.

items.title: Section: A Careful Paradox — Undefiled Relative to What Follows, Yet Still Falling Within Defiled Conduct

items.zh: 彼第八住一向清淨，此第七住猶名為雜。與清淨住為前導故，當言此住名不染污；猶未得故，當言此住墮雜染污。今此住中，一切貪等上首煩惱皆悉除斷。當知此住非有煩惱，非離煩惱。一切煩惱不現行故，悕求佛智猶未得故。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: establishing defiled and undefiled; first, viewed against the eighth abode. That eighth abode is uniformly pure; this seventh abode is still called mixed. Because it serves as forerunner to that pure abode, this abode should be called undefiled; because that purity is not yet attained, this abode should be said to fall within defiled conduct.
Second, viewed solely in terms of this abode. Within this abode, every ringleading affliction such as craving is entirely eliminated and severed. One should understand this abode as neither possessing affliction nor free of affliction. No affliction manifests at all, and yet the wisdom of the buddhas longed for has still not been attained.
Commentary: Regarding "the wisdom of the buddhas longed for has still not been attained" — this explains the earlier statement "not free of affliction." Because of still having applied effort, still having effortful application, the purity of the markless has not yet been genuinely realised.

items.title: Section: Teacher to the Entire Trichiliocosm — Unmatched by Any Save Bodhisattvas of the Eighth Ground and Beyond

items.zh: 如是行者，增上意樂已得清淨，無量身語意業隨轉，於諸如來所讚毀業，如前廣說。於第五住所引世間工巧業智轉得圓滿。三千世界共許為師，唯除安住上住菩薩及諸如來，意樂加行無與等者。
items.en: Sixth aspect: pure conduct and worldly craft both reaching complete fulfilment. Such a practitioner's heightened aspiration has attained purity, immeasurable bodily, verbal, and mental karma following accordingly. Regarding what the Tathāgatas praise and condemn, exactly as already explained at length, the worldly craft and skilful learning drawn forth at the fifth abode now turns genuinely complete and perfect. The entire trichiliocosm, by common consent, acknowledges this bodhisattva as teacher — excepting only bodhisattvas abiding at a higher ground and the tathāgatas themselves — no one else's aspiration and applied effort proving equal.

items.title: Section: Immeasurable, Uncommon Absorption — Still Cultivated Through Effort, Yet Already Surpassing Every Hearer and Solitary-Realiser

items.zh: 於一切靜慮等菩提分法皆能現前，由修行相現在前故，非由安住異熟分位，如第八住。此諸菩薩如是方便，能善思擇諸三摩地，引發菩薩三摩地上首十百千種三摩地門。由得如是三摩地故，超過一切聲聞、獨覺三摩地境。菩薩如是一切煩惱皆悉遠離；難可了知一切分別現行隨逐身語意業皆悉安住；而不捨離尋求勝進勇猛加行，顧念有情。為大菩提速圓滿故，離一切相無量身語意業隨轉，妙善修治無生法忍之所顯發。於此住中，由自覺慧境界故，超過一切聲聞、獨覺境界；餘六住中，但由佛法增上所緣故，超過一切聲聞、獨覺境界。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: attaining immeasurable, uncommon absorption; first, distinguishing the mark of attainment. Regarding every meditative absorption belonging to the factors of awakening, one is able to bring all directly to presence, through the mark of active cultivation becoming directly present — not through abiding in a ripened, resultant state, as at the eighth abode.
Second, displaying its immeasurability. Such bodhisattvas, through skilful means of this kind, are well able to discern among meditative absorptions, drawing forth foremost gates of bodhisattva absorption numbering in the tens, hundreds, and thousands.
Third, clarifying what is uncommon; first, regarding absorption itself. By attaining absorption of this kind, one surpasses the entire domain of every hearer and solitary-realiser's own absorption.
Second, regarding the sphere of activity; first, distinguishing the sphere engaged. Such a bodhisattva, every affliction entirely departed from; yet possessing an extremely subtle, difficult-to-discern discriminating activity following bodily, verbal, and mental karma, abiding in all of this; and never abandoning the pursuit of ever-greater advancement, courageous applied effort, and heartfelt regard for sentient beings.
Second, distinguishing this from the earlier grounds. Within this abode, by the very object of one's own awakened wisdom, one surpasses the entire domain of every hearer and solitary-realiser. Within the remaining six abodes, it was solely through buddha-dharma as one's heightened object of concern that one surpassed the entire domain of every hearer and solitary-realiser.

items.title: Section: Entering Cessation in Every Instant, Yet Never Certifying It — the Astonishing, Inconceivable Undertaking

items.zh: 又諸菩薩第六住中所入滅定，今此住中念念能入。然此菩薩甚希奇業不可思議。謂常安住實際住中，而於寂滅能不作證。
items.en:
Eighth aspect: entering the attainment of cessation in every single instant. Furthermore, whereas bodhisattvas at the sixth abode were able to enter the attainment of cessation, bodhisattvas at this abode are able to enter it in every single instant of mind. And yet these bodhisattvas' own undertaking is astonishing, inconceivable — constantly abiding within the very state of ultimate reality, while never actually certifying that same quiescent cessation.
Commentary: Regarding "the attainment of cessation entered at the sixth abode" and the like — the sutra says: a bodhisattva, from the sixth ground onward, is able to enter the attainment of quiescent cessation; now, abiding at the seventh bodhisattva ground, in every single instant one is able to enter the attainment of quiescent cessation, and yet does not certify that same quiescent cessation — this bodhisattva ultimately accomplishing inconceivable bodily, verbal, and mental karma. This should be understood accordingly.

blocks.text: The seventh ground is the last that still needs effort. The treatise describes it as a careful paradox: no affliction appears, yet it is "not purely pure".
Master Cháng Bǎi: diligent effort is "adding", laziness "subtracting"; the seventh ground aims at effortless practice.
Master Cháng Bǎi: they come down to seeking awakening above and transforming beings below.
"In every single instant of mind, the ten perfections foremost, every factor of awakening is completely fulfilled; lower grounds are not so."

"Because no affliction manifests, and because buddha-wisdom is sought but not yet attained." Master Cháng Bǎi: in absorption it accords with the markless, but not necessarily outside it; beyond a certain point, great effort becomes an obstacle. A small part of the cognitive obscuration remains. Venerable Miào Jìng: something is still grasped.
Master Cháng Bǎi: all beings of the trichiliocosm acknowledge this bodhisattva as teacher, yet still grasping something in saving beings is what the Buddha rebukes.
"Here, by one's own awakened wisdom; in the other six grounds, only by taking the buddha-dharma as object." Venerable Miào Jìng: at the eighth ground the markless appears naturally.
Venerable Miào Jìng: cessation here is really suchness; within quiescence, without leaving it, deportment manifests. Master Cháng Bǎi: the water is there to drink, yet one does not drink it.
"Beyond a certain point, great effort becomes an obstacle." Every practitioner meets a version of this: the effort that got you here is what must be relaxed to go further.

quiz.q: In the seventh ground's "with effort (加行)," how do the lectures explain 加?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: diligent effort is "adding," laziness "subtracting"; the seventh ground aims at effortless practice. Venerable Miào Jìng: "加" means not being lazy — laziness is subtracting.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi summarise the ten "places" of the uncommon excellent conduct?
options: the ten places reduce to two — seeking awakening above, transforming beings below
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ten places come down to seeking awakening above and transforming beings below. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first phrase is general, the rest specific.

quiz.q: At the seventh abode, what happens in every instant, and how do lower grounds compare?
options: the ten perfections foremost, all factors of awakening complete; lower grounds are not so
quiz.why: "In every single instant of mind, the ten perfections foremost, every factor of awakening is completely fulfilled; lower grounds are not so." Master Cháng Bǎi: in whatever instant, the ten perfections are complete.

quiz.q: The seventh abode is "undefiled" yet "falls within defiled conduct." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this mixture?
options: in absorption it accords with marklessness, not necessarily outside; beyond a point, striving itself becomes an obstacle
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in absorption it accords with the markless, but not necessarily outside it; beyond a certain point, great effort becomes an obstacle. Venerable Miào Jìng: not purely pure — something is still grasped.

quiz.q: Why is the seventh abode "neither with nor free of affliction"?
options: no affliction manifests (so not "with"); buddha-wisdom is sought but not yet attained (so not "free")
quiz.why: "Because no affliction manifests, and because buddha-wisdom is sought but not yet attained." Master Cháng Bǎi: none of the afflictions of saṃsāra manifest, but a small part of the cognitive obscuration remains.

quiz.q: The seventh-ground bodhisattva is "teacher to the trichiliocosm." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say the Buddha would still rebuke?
options: still grasping something in saving beings — a trace of attachment
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: still grasping something in saving beings — which the Buddha rebukes; all beings of the trichiliocosm acknowledge this one as teacher of gods and humans. Venerable Miào Jìng: subtle affliction is grasping — some attachment remains.

quiz.q: "Through active cultivation, not through a ripened state as at the eighth." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: "ripening" means spontaneous; at the eighth ground it appears effortlessly
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "ripening" means natural — the seventh ground doesn't yet abide in that natural state; at the eighth, Immovable, it appears spontaneously.

quiz.q: How does the seventh ground surpass śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha domains differently from the first six?
options: the seventh by its own awakened wisdom; the other six only by the dharma as object
quiz.why: "Here, by one's own awakened wisdom; in the other six, only by taking the buddha-dharma as object." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first six surpass by object, not by wisdom.

quiz.q: "Entering cessation in every instant, yet not certifying it." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: cessation here is suchness — manifesting deportment without leaving it; Cháng Bǎi: the dharma-water is fully drinkable, yet one doesn't drink
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: cessation here is really suchness; within quiescence, without leaving it, deportment manifests. Master Cháng Bǎi: the water is there to drink, yet one doesn't — the dharma-water fully available, yet not drunk.
